transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-12-17
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Luis Ortega (Redwood SE), Daniel Roberts (StratusHealth VP Legal), Sana Idris (Procurement), Evan Park (CTO), Monica Lee (Head of Security), Tom Alvarez (Integration)

Summary (auto): Procurement / legal alignment on MSA/DPA, SLA metrics, pricing approval path, onboarding tasks. Action items captured.

00:00:05 - Maya Chen: hey everyone, thanks for making time today, we wanted to run through the MSA and DPA redlines and also make sure we have the onboarding checklist and PO timing, i'll hand it over to daniel to start -
00:00:22 - Daniel Roberts: yeah thanks maya, quick note from legal, we have a couple concern points in the DPA around subprocessor lists and data retention in third-party systems, also want clarity on audit rights and encryption at rest, um
00:00:41 - Luis Ortega: sure, on the subprocessor side we can provide the current list and commit to notifying you for material changes; for encryption we use customer-managed KMS options in dedicated/private setups, and hosted customers can opt into our KMS integration, there are HSM-backed options too -
00:01:05 - Monica Lee: can you clarify the KMS workflow, is that full key control or just envelope encryption?
00:01:18 - Luis Ortega: it's envelope + customer key material option in the Private deployment, for hosted we can offer customer-managed keys depending on the contract, i will share the integration doc, apologies the product name in older docs says Red wood dedicated, that's our internal older naming, it's Redwood inference runtime -
00:01:44 - Sana Idris: procurement here, timeline wise we need the redlined MSA + DPA by this Friday to route for approval, and an itemized pricing sheet to attach to PO, is that doable?
00:01:59 - Maya Chen: yes, we can get redlines over by Friday; we'll also include a pricing workbook showing hosted vs dedicated unit economics and committed tiers, we'll flag the recommended plan for your workload -
00:02:18 - Evan Park: from an engineering POV, we are leaning to a hybrid approach: start hosted for quick rollout, then move critical workloads to Dedicated or Private for data residency. We need p95 latency targets and cost numbers for both.
00:02:35 - Luis Ortega: absolutely, i'll include p50/p95 latency numbers from similar healthcare customers and a cost delta table; usually dedicated gives you about 30-40% lower per-token cost at steady throughput, but startup burst costs differ -
00:02:52 - Tom Alvarez: and for network, we need VPC peering or private link details, plus Cidr ranges for the connectors, we'll share ours after call -
00:03:07 - Maya Chen: perfect, tom, add that to the onboarding checklist, we'll want an SSO window too for SAML setup -
00:03:22 - Daniel Roberts: on SLAs, legal wants an uptime SLA and remediation credits, and something about rollback / fallback if model regressions occur that materially impact output quality, is that something you cover?
00:03:37 - Luis Ortega: we have SLOs per route and can provide A/B rollback policies and version pinning; for SLAs we typically do 99.9% availability on dedicated with credit schedules, hosted we have tiered SLAs in enterprise plans, i'll include the exact SLA clause and propose language you can review -
00:03:56 - Monica Lee: audit logs—we need immutable audit trails for all calls and admin actions, retention 7 years is ideal for us, what are retention options?
00:04:12 - Maya Chen: we can extend observability retention as an add-on, default is 90 days but enterprise add-ons get longer retention and we can include log export to your S3 for long term archival -
00:04:29 - Daniel Roberts: can we get a copy of your SOC2 and ISO coverage and the DPA template?
00:04:37 - Maya Chen: yes, i'll attach SOC2 report and the DPA template in the follow-up email, we'll also send the redline-ready doc -
00:04:52 - 00:05:10 - [silence / minor crosstalk] -
00:05:12 - Luis Ortega: quick techncial note, for privacy-sensitive workloads we recommend using Private (VPC) deployments with customer-managed KMS; this avoids egress and residency concerns. If you want to pilot, we can provide a short-term isolated cluster -
00:05:35 - Sana Idris: that would help accelerate legal sign-off if they can see the private option operational, yes -
00:05:49 - Maya Chen: okay on pricing approvals—do you have an internal approval threshold? is it a head of procurement for all deals or does finance need to review?
00:06:03 - Sana Idris: finance reviews over $100k annual commit, below that procurement can sign off; this deal will likely be in the 150-250k range once we scope the dedicated footprint -
00:06:19 - Evan Park: add to that we need a trial phase for 3 weeks with representative traffic and prompt sets, we want to validate latency and cost under realistic sessions -
00:06:32 - Luis Ortega: we can do a 3-week trial with a dedicated pilot region, we'll need a small commit and infra access; i'll prepare a benchmark plan with simulated prompt sets and drop in your prompt corpus -
00:06:48 - 00:07:10 - [laughter / agreement] -
00:07:12 - Daniel Roberts: about liability caps and indemnity, our legal team will propose some tweaks; we prefer mutual caps tied to fees, not broad carveouts -
00:07:27 - Maya Chen: noted, we often negotiate that to be mutual and proportional, we'll leave those as redline items for your counsel -
00:07:41 - Monica Lee: encryption in transit, can you confirm TLS versions and cert management? we also want support for mTLS for internal backends -
00:07:55 - Luis Ortega: TLS 1.2+ supported, certificate management via standard CA and mTLS support in Private/Dedicated. i'll include an architecture diagram in the follow-up -
00:08:12 - Tom Alvarez: operational runbooks—do you provide runbooks for incident response and failover to fallback models? we need to plug that into our DR plan -
00:08:25 - Luis Ortega: yep, we have incident runbooks, model fallback policies (route to smaller model variant automatically), and can supply a customized DR runbook as part of the Dedicated onboarding -
00:08:42 - 00:09:10 - [brief pause as doc is shared over chat] -
00:09:12 - Maya Chen: i'll walk through the timeline we propose: send MSA/DPA redlines by Friday, procurement to route PO, LOE for onboarding 2-3 weeks, pilot 3 weeks after infra access, then roll to dedicated for critical workloads, does that align?
00:09:33 - Sana Idris: that aligns, we'll aim to have approvals by next Tuesday if redlines are clean -
00:09:46 - Daniel Roberts: one more ask, can Redwood add a clause for periodic compliance attestations annually and prior notice of subprocessor changes?
00:09:58 - Maya Chen: yes we can add those clauses, we'll mark them in the redline and propose notification windows (30 days for material subprocessor changes) -
00:10:12 - 00:10:40 - [brief crosstalk re: document editing tools] -
00:10:42 - Luis Ortega: on the performance numbers, quick preview: for similar telehealth traffic we see p95 sub-400ms on dedicated for chat-style models with KV cache enabled; hosted numbers vary by region and burst -
00:11:00 - Evan Park: is KV cache compatible with your multi-tenant hosted offering? we can't share patient tokens in shared cache -
00:11:12 - Luis Ortega: for PHI we recommend Private or Dedicated with per-customer KV isolation; hosted has prefix caching but not per-customer isolated KV by default -
00:11:29 - Monica Lee: PHI handling is critical, we need a written affirmation that we can support HIPAA-covered workflows under Private and Dedicated.
00:11:41 - Maya Chen: yes, we support HIPAA BAA in Private/Dedicated; i'll attach the BAA template and HIPAA scope docs -
00:11:52 - 00:12:20 - [short pause] -
00:12:22 - Daniel Roberts: ok on pricing — can you provide a committed capacity quote vs pay-as-you-go so finance can model both? also show breakpoints for 1yr vs 3yr terms -
00:12:38 - Maya Chen: we'll provide a pricing workbook with committed discounts and examples for 1/3 year terms, include an amortized per-token number and estimated monthly spend based on your forecast -
00:12:52 - Sana Idris: procurement will also need approved PO language and bank details, can those be in the pricing pack?
00:12:59 - Maya Chen: yes, we'll include billing instructions and PO templates -
00:13:12 - 00:13:45 - [minor typing / chat notes] -
00:13:48 - Tom Alvarez: integrations question: what SDKs and observability hooks exist? we want trace IDs, per-request metadata, and token-level cost breakdown -
00:14:02 - Luis Ortega: SDKs for python/node/java, and we expose trace headers and token accounting in the logs; Console shows token-level cost and latency per-route -
00:14:17 - Evan Park: do you support function/tool calling or structured output enforcement for our triage flows?
00:14:28 - Luis Ortega: yes we support structured responses and function-calling patterns, we'll share examples from existing health customers (with sanitized prompts) -
00:14:40 - 00:15:05 - [screen share: onboarding checklist] -
00:15:07 - Maya Chen: shifting to next steps: action items captured, i'll send the docs and schedule a kickoff once PO is in place, are there any blockers we haven't surfaced?
00:15:22 - Daniel Roberts: just legal redlines and confirming the BAA/hipaa scope, otherwise timeline looks fine -
00:15:34 - Sana Idris: procurement might ask for net-60 billing terms, is that something you all accept?
00:15:45 - Maya Chen: our standard is net-30 for self-serve; enterprise deals can do net-60 after credit review, we'll flag for finance -
00:15:58 - Evan Park: one technical ask: can we get a short latency runbook for cold-start mitigation and KV eviction policies?
00:16:10 - Luis Ortega: yes i'll include operational tuning guidance for cold starts, batching, kv cache TTL recommendations -
00:16:26 - 00:16:50 - [brief chatter about scheduling follow-ups] -
00:16:52 - Maya Chen: ok final recap: Maya sends redlines + SOC2 + pricing workbook by Friday, Luis sends benchmark plan and performance sheet, Tom provides VPC CIDR and an environment contact, Sana confirms PO routing timeline -
00:17:12 - Daniel Roberts: that works, thanks everyone -
00:17:18 - Maya Chen: thanks, we'll follow up with an email and folder with artifacts -
00:17:26 - 00:17:40 - [meeting ends; remaining minutes used for chat clarifications and doc sharing]
